The chemical register update is within my ability to initiate, but it requires the revised SDS to be formally processed through our chemical-management system, which I have not yet started. The labeled segregated storage requires physical setup in or near the materials cage and verification by me before I can record it. The hazardous-waste manifest procedures require coordination with our waste-handling protocols and documentation that does not currently exist for this material. I want to be straightforward — I am not in a position to commit to a timeline without assessing each of these in detail, and I do not want to give the group false confidence that Thursday is achievable if it is not. What I can commit to is beginning immediately on all three items if you direct me to proceed. I would also note that even if I complete the chemical register update and storage verification, the hazardous-waste manifest procedures for discarded pellets and purge material during the run itself will need to be in place before production starts — not after. If the group or anyone here has information about resources or personnel available to support the storage setup and manifest documentation on an expedited basis, that would help me give you a realistic answer on Thursday feasibility.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Attach lab review results including 15%-to-85% blend ratio and FTIR first-article testing requirement for first 50 housings to the production traveler before any future authorization.

If directed to proceed in preparation for future authorization: enter revised SDS in chemical register, verify and record labeled segregated storage for reclaimed lot, and establish hazardous-waste manifest procedures for discarded pellets and purge material.

Address the virgin polymer shortfall through alternative means — additional virgin polymer procurement, batch size reduction, or run rescheduling — since reclaimed material cannot be authorized without completed environmental-compliance sign-off.
